title: GauPRE: A Pattern-based Rendering Engine for Gaussian Splatting on Edge Device
problem: 3D Gaussian Splatting rendering on edge devices (~10FPS) fails to achieve real-time (≥30FPS) performance due to computational constraints; Gauss-Tile rasterization bottleneck stems from decoupled nature and computation-accuracy tradeoffs that current hardware cannot effectively address.
motivation: 3DGS offers excellent visual quality for AR/VR but edge deployment requires real-time performance; rasterization efficiency is critical for mobile 3D rendering.
method: Software-hardware co-design with pattern-based rasterization: flood encoding represents tile coverage efficiently, pattern-aware rasterization unit (PRU) with k-means codebook compression preserves accuracy with minimal area. GPU integration with early depth-sorting and tile-group-wise rasterization fuses coverage testing and alpha blending into seamless dataflow.
key_novelty: Pattern-based tile rasterization combining flood encoding and codebook compression for efficient 3DGS rendering on resource-constrained edge devices.
contributions: Pattern-aware rasterization unit (PRU) with efficient tile coverage representation
11.6× end-to-end speedup on Jetson Orin Nano vs. baseline
2.09× higher rasterization throughput vs. SOTA 3DGS accelerator
limitations: Evaluation limited to Jetson Orin Nano platform; applicability to other edge devices unclear; visual quality metrics not quantified; compression impact on rendering quality not analyzed.
